item.title: Spain refers LaLiga chief to tribunal over Real Madrid Nazi comments
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye LaLiga president Javier Tebas has been referred to Spain’s sports tribunal over his comparison of Real Madrid’s communication tactics to Nazi propaganda, following the Spanish club’s demand for his resignation. According to Reuters, Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) announced on Thursday that it had referred Tebas to the Administrative Court for Sport (TAD) to determine whether his remarks breached regulations protecting sporting dignity and decorum. The referral concerns comments Tebas made on social media on October 16, criticising Real Madrid’s handling of complaints about refereeing decisions and the club’s television coverage of match officials. Tebas accused Real Madrid of using communication tactics that recalled propaganda methods employed by Joseph Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister. Real Madrid subsequently demanded the immediate resignation of the 64-year-old, describing his comparison as unacceptable for someone holding the position of LaLiga president. However, Tebas insisted that he was referring to propaganda techniques rather than Nazi ideology or Real Madrid’s supporters. In its referral, the CSD asked the tribunal to assess whether the remarks could constitute a serious offence under Article 76.4.b of Spain’s 1990 Sports Law, which covers public acts that infringe upon sporting dignity or decorum. Possible sanctions for such offences include warnings, fines or suspension. The controversy followed Tebas’s criticism of Real Madrid’s efforts to challenge the standard of refereeing in Spanish football. The club has repeatedly questioned officiating decisions through its in-house television channel. In a fresh post on X on Thursday, Tebas defended his comments and questioned why Real Madrid’s accusations against Spanish referees had not attracted similar scrutiny under the rules governing sporting dignity. “Defending the competition also requires responding to those who constantly discredit it,” Tebas wrote, adding that he intended to continue exercising that responsibility. He also argued that Real Madrid’s repeated questioning of the integrity of Spanish football could itself be examined under the same rules. The AFP also reports that the CSD emphasised the importance of protecting respect, coexistence and fair play in sport. The tribunal will determine whether the matter warrants disciplinary proceedings. No finding of wrongdoing against Tebas has been announced. item.title: DSS arrests 23-year-old female arms courier in Nasarawa
item.description: — Sule commends security agencies over crackdown on arms trafficking By Edwin Philip LAFIA — Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, has commended the Department of State Services (DSS) for its sustained efforts to clamp down on gun runners and arms traffickers in the state following the arrest of a 23-year-old female suspected arms courier in Keffi. The governor’s commendation was contained in a statement issued on Thursday by his Press Secretary, Ibrahim Addra, who described the arrest of Aisha Mohammed, a resident of Bwari, Federal Capital Territory, as a significant breakthrough. According to the statement, Mohammed was arrested with 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition and three empty magazines. “The suspect, currently in custody, was arrested while in possession of 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition with three empty magazines,” the statement said. It added that other suspected arms couriers arrested between August and September 2026 included Hassan Sani, 40; Abdulkadir Idrissa, 41; and Salihu Garba, 70, also known as Nabayi. The statement said security operatives recovered 678 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, 99 rounds of 7.5mm ammunition and other items from the suspects. It further disclosed that an alleged arms courier, Ismail Lawalli, a native of Zamfara State, was arrested in August along the Keffi-Abuja highway with 1,262 assorted rounds of ammunition. Sule praised DSS personnel and other security agencies in Nasarawa for their dedication and commitment to tackling arms trafficking and other criminal activities. He also commended the collaboration between the security agencies and his administration, pledging continued government support for their operations. The governor assured residents of his administration’s resolve to combat criminality and called on the public to support security agencies in maintaining peace and safety across the state. These are important details that help establish the identity and traceability of a product,” she said. item.title: Lawal swears in five permanent secretaries
item.description: — Charges appointees to uphold public service rules, financial regulations By Idris Salisu GUSAU — Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has sworn in five new permanent secretaries into the state civil service, charging them to comply with public service rules, financial regulations and other relevant laws. The swearing-in ceremony took place on Thursday at the Grand Chamber of the Government House in Gusau, with the Chief Judge of the state, Justice Kulu Aliyu, administering the oath of office. The new permanent secretaries are Ahmad S. Zamfara, Nasiru Halilu Anka, Mu’azu Jibril Guraguri, Adamu Abdullahi Kanoma and Sani Muhammad Shinkafi. Speaking at the ceremony, Lawal said the appointments reflected confidence in the officers’ experience, abilities and readiness to assume greater responsibilities in the state’s administration. He said permanent secretaries played a critical role in providing administrative leadership, ensuring institutional continuity, advising on policy implementation and maintaining discipline within the civil service. “Becoming permanent secretaries is more than personal advancement: as senior administrative leaders, your decisions and conduct directly affect government performance and the welfare of the people we serve,” the governor said. Lawal said his administration remained committed to strengthening government institutions and improving public administration to support the state’s development agenda. He urged the appointees to ensure that government policies were backed by proper planning, realistic implementation strategies, effective supervision and continuous assessment of results. “Proper planning, realistic implementation strategies, effective supervision and continuous assessment of results must support policies and programmes,” he said. The governor also advised the permanent secretaries to maintain professional relationships with commissioners and other political officeholders, stressing the need for cooperation between political leaders and career civil servants. “Political leaders set policy; career civil servants provide the institutional knowledge, technical advice, and administrative capacity to implement it. These roles complement each other, and the effectiveness of the government depends on mutual respect,” he said. Lawal said the civil service remained central to translating government decisions into tangible results, particularly in the delivery of essential services and the implementation of reforms aimed at meeting the needs and aspirations of Zamfara residents. He urged the new permanent secretaries to approach their assignments with discipline, professionalism and a clear understanding of the administration’s priorities. FG mobilises states, resources As part of efforts to prevent a wider outbreak, the Federal Government said it had informed all state governments and directed those yet to complete their Ebola response plans to do so urgently. The minister disclosed that the government had mobilised additional resources for the response, including funds released by President Bola Tinubu to strengthen the capacity of the NCDC. He said the Presidential Task Force had been briefed, alongside the Nigeria Governors’ Forum and the National Economic Council, chaired by the Vice-President. “All state governments have been informed. Most states already have response plans developed with the guidance of the NCDC. We have directed those that are yet to complete their plans to do so urgently,” he said. The government is also adopting a whole-of-government approach involving the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Ministry of Aviation and other relevant agencies. The minister said a meeting with state commissioners of health and information was scheduled to strengthen coordination and ensure that public communication remained consistent across the country. He maintained that Nigeria’s public health system had demonstrated its capacity to respond swiftly, noting that authorities diagnosed and confirmed the case within 24 hours of notification and informed the World Health Organisation (WHO). “We are not starting from scratch,” he said, expressing confidence in the expertise of Nigerian health professionals and the investments made in public health preparedness. Experts to sequence virus The government has also initiated steps to sequence the virus’s genome to improve understanding of the strain involved and support the response. The minister said Professor Christian Happi, a renowned infectious disease genomics expert based at Redeemer University, Ede, had been invited to complement the work of the NCDC through the African Centre of Excellence for Genomics of Infectious Diseases. He said international partners, including WHO and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, were supporting the response, while experts with experience in managing outbreaks in other countries had arrived to assist Nigeria. The minister said the collaboration demonstrated the importance of strengthening local expertise and scientific capacity in responding to public health emergencies. FG steps up border screening The government also announced plans to intensify screening and preventive measures at Nigeria’s points of entry as part of efforts to reduce the risk of further imported infections. According to the minister, port health services had been strengthened, while additional capacity was being sought to improve screening and ensure that thermal imaging equipment was functional. He said the assessment of travellers would continue to be guided by risk categorisation and international health regulations. The minister disclosed that Nigeria had gone five months without recording a case despite substantial international travel, with more than 40,000 travellers entering the country during that period. He said the government would continue to strengthen border health measures, but stressed that the immediate priority remained containing the confirmed case and tracing all contacts. Hospitals, private clinics on alert Further, the Ali Pate said all federal hospitals had been notified and directed to ensure adequate bed capacity, functional isolation facilities and strict infection prevention and control measures. State governments were also urged to prepare their hospitals and ensure that health workers were trained and adequately equipped to identify and manage suspected cases. He particularly emphasised the role of private healthcare providers, noting that the patient had visited a private medical facility before the infection was confirmed. “The private sector is equally important because the patient visited a private health facility. item.title: 2027: OBJ’s son joins ‘Tinubu Must Stay’ movement, backs reform continuity
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Son of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, Olujonwo, has joined the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as the “Tinubu Must Stay” movement, to promote what he described as policy continuity and public understanding of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Olujonwo, who serves as President of the Buhari Youth Organisation BYO, President of Project One Nigeria, and Senior Special Assistant to the Ogun State Governor on Housing, was officially received by TMS leadership at a fora in Abuja. Explaining his decision, Olujonwo stated that his long-standing alignment with the ruling party and his understanding of Nigeria’s reform history informed his choice to join the movement. “I have been in the APC since 2014. I was there when my father hosted the late President Muhammadu Buhari and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to form the movement. I am not new to the party,” he said. He noted that critical achievements of the current administration are being distorted by public misinformation, creating a need for clearer communication regarding key government policies. “There is a lot of noise out there, and people are distorting what is going on. ASUU has had no strikes. Students have access to loans. Nigeria has become a massive construction site and an investors’ haven again. These are things we need to promote,” he said. Welcoming him to the platform, the National Coordinator of TMS and Director General of the National Information Technology Development Agency NITDA, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, stated that Olujonwo’s background equips him to appreciate the necessity of economic reforms. Makinde made the call on Thursday at the APM Southwest Town Hall held at the Ondo State International Conference Centre, The Dome, in Akure, where he presented his Reset Nigeria agenda as a pathway to national renewal. He described the Southwest as a historic vanguard of Nigeria’s progress, arguing that the region must once again take the lead in shaping the country’s political and economic future. The governor dismissed suggestions that the Southwest should not produce another presidential candidate because the region currently holds the presidency. He cited the 1999 presidential election, when former President Olusegun Obasanjo and Olu Falae contested for the country’s highest office without controversy. item.title: 2027: INEC deploys AI to check election result figures before upload

The chatbot provides government information in English, Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba, a model she said could be adapted to help voters access reliable information about registration, polling units and election procedures. “Build something that makes the truth easier to find than falsehood,” she challenged developers. The programme’s convener, Dr Toyosi Akerele-Ogunsiji, said the initiative would bring together developers, researchers, journalists, election experts and civil society organisations to build functional solutions to electoral challenges ahead of 2027. She said the programme followed the development of Run-Am, an AI-powered misinformation detection and fact-checking application created for Nigeria’s 2023 elections. The new initiative will focus on trustworthy electoral information, data analysis, inclusive and multilingual civic technology, cybersecurity, election observation and citizen accountability. It will also include an AI Innovations Development Hub and a Community of Practice to support promising solutions beyond the hackathon. Applications opened on Thursday, October 22, and will close on November 12, 2026. Eligible Nigerians aged 18 and above may apply individually or in teams of up to four. The competition has a N10 million prize pool, with N4 million for the overall winner, N2.5 million for second place and N1.5 million for third place, alongside four special awards worth N500,000 each. Professor Victor Odumuyiwa of the University of Lagos urged INEC to prioritise homegrown solutions, arguing that Nigerian developers were better placed to understand the country’s electoral challenges. “We understand our context, we know the problems, and we are the ones best placed to solve them,” he said. Lawyer Tsema Ede, who addressed the legal and ethical implications of AI in elections, said the technology offered opportunities for voter education, electoral malpractice monitoring and cybersecurity but required safeguards against misuse. The organisers said the programme would remain non-partisan, barring projects designed to influence voter preferences or interfere with electoral administration. Unauthorised testing of live electoral systems is also prohibited, while winning the competition will not automatically authorise operational deployment. The initiative will culminate in a national grand finale in Lagos on December 16, followed by technical support for selected innovations. Makinde, who spoke at the APM South-West town hall meeting in Akure, Ondo State, said Nigeria was not functioning as it should, blaming weak budget implementation and an unproductive economy for the country’s persistent challenges. He said the contest demonstrated that the South-West could present multiple candidates and allow Nigerians to choose their preferred leader. “In 1999, when the entire country ceded the presidency to the South-West, we had two of our fathers, Baba President Olusegun Obasanjo and Baba Olu Falae, contesting for the presidency. Both were from the South-West, and heaven did not fall,” he said. Makinde added that Nigeria’s challenges required collective action across regions, rather than an approach based on political entitlement or the belief that a particular region should automatically retain power. He also criticised what he described as the use of political power to weaken opposition parties, insisting that a functioning democracy required an open political space. “I do not understand how a party in power, with 31 governors and almost all the instruments of coercion at its disposal, can still be afraid of the opposition. It will not allow the opposition to thrive,” he said. He called on the Federal Government to stop actions that he alleged were creating crises for opposition parties, adding that “there is no democracy in a one-party system.” Security, economic reforms On security, Makinde said Nigeria needed to overhaul its security architecture to create an environment in which businesses could operate beyond the current constraints imposed by insecurity. Makinde also reiterated his call for the Federal Government to remit funds due to states and local governments from the Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) revenue, saying the reconciliation of the figures had been completed. He said the Reset Nigeria agenda would seek to make the economy more productive and create multiple pathways for lifting citizens out of poverty. The APM candidate urged South-West residents to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and support his presidential ambition, describing himself as a “reset agent”. He also proposed that an APM-led administration would constitute a transitional government of national unity to reposition the country for prosperity. APM offers alternative Earlier, the party’s National Chairman, Mamman Dantalle, said the APM was offering Nigerians an alternative to the country’s current political and economic direction ahead of the 2027 general election. He identified insecurity as a major national concern, saying many Nigerians were afraid of travelling, visiting markets or going to their farms because of the risk of kidnapping. The party chairman argued that insecurity was linked to broader socio-economic problems, including poverty, inequality, poor living conditions and hopelessness. “These kidnappers are not unknown individuals. They live among us. They are our brothers. They are our family members. They are our friends,” he said. He added that some conventional crimes reflected deeper problems in the country’s socio-economic and political arrangements. “Sociologically, some of these conventional crimes are not the problem. They are only indications that something is wrong with the socio-economic and political arrangement. And what is that? Inequality, poverty, squalor and hopelessness,” he said. Also speaking, Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed said Nigeria needed leaders with the vision, knowledge and capacity to unlock the potential of its different regions. Mohammed highlighted the economic importance of the South-South, particularly its natural resources, but said the region required leadership capable of translating its wealth into improved living standards. He said the APM candidates offered an opportunity to pursue a different direction through planning, consultation and public participation. item.description: — Sanwo-Olu, Obasa, Ojelabi, Edun urge grassroots mobilisation By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Convener of the Lagos4Lagos Movement, Olajide Adediran, popularly known as Jandor, has inaugurated a support group for President Bola Tinubu, Lagos State governorship candidate Dr Obafemi Hamzat and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates, targeting more than three million votes for the party in the state in the 2027 elections. The JANDOR Support Group for PBAT-KOH 2027 was inaugurated on Thursday at the Eko FM Marquee, Lagos Television premises, Agidingbi, Ikeja, with party leaders, local government chairmen, traditional rulers and members of the Lagos4Lagos Movement in attendance. Adediran, the group’s lead visioner, said the initiative was established to fulfil his commitment to support whoever emerged as the APC’s candidate and contribute to the party’s electoral mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Speaking to journalists after the inauguration, Jandor said the move followed his withdrawal from the Lagos governorship race after the party’s candidate-selection process. He said the Lagos4Lagos Movement’s structure had been aligned with the APC from the state executive level to senatorial districts, local governments and wards. According to him, two representatives from each polling unit would be inaugurated separately at the local-government level to canvass support for APC candidates in the presidential and governorship elections. Adediran stressed that the group was designed to complement, not compete with, the party’s main campaign council. He urged members to respect the party’s leadership structure and persuade voters through peaceful engagement rather than intimidation or insults. The former governorship aspirant also called on members to place the party’s collective interest above personal ambitions and extend mobilisation to markets, motor parks, workplaces, religious communities and neighbourhoods. “That declaration was not made casually. item.content:encoded: — Sanwo-Olu, Obasa, Ojelabi, Edun urge grassroots mobilisation By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Convener of the Lagos4Lagos Movement, Olajide Adediran, popularly known as Jandor, has inaugurated a support group for President Bola Tinubu, Lagos State governorship candidate Dr Obafemi Hamzat and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates, targeting more than three million votes for the party in the state in the 2027 elections. The JANDOR Support Group for PBAT-KOH 2027 was inaugurated on Thursday at the Eko FM Marquee, Lagos Television premises, Agidingbi, Ikeja, with party leaders, local government chairmen, traditional rulers and members of the Lagos4Lagos Movement in attendance. Adediran, the group’s lead visioner, said the initiative was established to fulfil his commitment to support whoever emerged as the APC’s candidate and contribute to the party’s electoral mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Speaking to journalists after the inauguration, Jandor said the move followed his withdrawal from the Lagos governorship race after the party’s candidate-selection process. He said the Lagos4Lagos Movement’s structure had been aligned with the APC from the state executive level to senatorial districts, local governments and wards. According to him, two representatives from each polling unit would be inaugurated separately at the local-government level to canvass support for APC candidates in the presidential and governorship elections. Adediran stressed that the group was designed to complement, not compete with, the party’s main campaign council. He urged members to respect the party’s leadership structure and persuade voters through peaceful engagement rather than intimidation or insults. The former governorship aspirant also called on members to place the party’s collective interest above personal ambitions and extend mobilisation to markets, motor parks, workplaces, religious communities and neighbourhoods. “That declaration was not made casually. It was a statement of our belief in party supremacy, internal democracy, discipline and the greater interest of our political family,” he said, referring to his earlier commitment to support the party after the selection of its candidate. He added that although party members could have different ambitions and opinions during the candidate-selection process, the party’s decision should take precedence once the process was concluded. “We are therefore here today to honour that promise,” he said. Adediran reiterated that the support group would not operate as a parallel campaign structure. “Let me state this unequivocally: JANDOR Support Group for PBAT-KOH is a complementary mobilisation structure, not a parallel campaign council. “We are not setting up another authority to compete with the existing one. We are building additional hands to support a common mission,” he said. He pledged that the group would cooperate with the main campaign council and follow the party’s overall campaign direction, while using its grassroots network to widen voter engagement. Three-million-vote target The chairman of Ibeju-Lekki Local Council Development Area and chairman of the association of council chairmen in Lagos, Sesan Olowa, pledged the support of chairmen across the state’s 20 local government areas and 37 local council development areas for Tinubu, Hamzat and other APC candidates. Olowa urged the new group to work alongside existing campaign structures, stressing that cooperation was necessary to avoid duplication and internal competition. He announced a target of more than three million votes for the APC in Lagos and called for mobilisation across the state’s 13,325 polling units. He also urged the group to engage residents across communities and ensure that its campaign reached voters at the grassroots. Former Minister of Finance, Wale Edun, commended Jandor for keeping his promise to support the party after withdrawing from the governorship contest. Edun described grassroots mobilisation as important to electoral participation and encouraged supporters to engage registered voters in their communities. He also urged political stakeholders to contribute their time and resources to party activities, saying political participation required consistent engagement beyond attending meetings. Sanwo-Olu, Ojelabi urge cooperation Representing Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, his Chief of Staff and state coordinator of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors, Tayo Ayinde, urged members to conduct their activities peacefully and in accordance with party directives. Ayinde said the Lagos4Lagos Movement’s grassroots network could strengthen the APC’s mobilisation efforts ahead of the 2027 elections. He urged coordinators to avoid factional disputes, maintain contact with residents and communicate the policies and programmes of the federal and state governments. Ayinde also reiterated the three-million-vote target, urging members to sustain community engagement and follow the timetable for electoral activities. The Lagos APC chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi, formally inaugurated the group and called on its members to work with existing party structures. Ojelabi praised Adediran for honouring his commitment to support the APC after the governorship candidate-selection process, adding that the initiative could provide more party members with opportunities to contribute to mobilisation. He urged the group’s coordinators to work with party structures at ward and polling-unit levels and engage community development associations. Another speaker at the event stressed the need for political leaders to invest in grassroots structures and demonstrate their capacity to mobilise support at polling-unit, ward and local-government levels. The inauguration marked the formal commencement of the support group’s activities. Adediran said the next phase would involve inaugurating its polling-unit representatives across local governments. Other guests included former Oriade LCDA chairman, Ramota Akinola-Hassan; chairman of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors in Mushin Local Government, E.O. Bamgboye; Oba Oloyede, the Oba of Onigbongbo; Oba Oluwasegun Ajasa; former Ojo Local Government chairman, Rasulu Idowu; and Vice Leader of the Apex Group of the Lagos4Lagos Movement, Alhaja Sofurat Abdulkareem. A promising economic indicator matters, but citizens want to know whether their lives are becoming more manageable,” he said. “The World Bank reported that Nigeria’s real GDP grew by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026. The Central Bank’s figures showed year-on-year headline inflation easing to 14.63 per cent in September from 15.39 per cent in August. “These are positive movements. But when inflation falls, prices may still be rising, only at a slower pace. It does not mean that the cost of living has returned to what families could afford before.” Speaking further, the media chief stated, “This distinction matters for public communication. If an official says that inflation has eased, and a family hears that food is still more expensive, the family is not being unreasonable. The two statements can both be true. Good leadership explains the difference and keeps working on the effect people actually feel. “Growth must mean more than a number. It must become decent jobs, dependable public services, wages that can support a household, opportunity for young people, and confidence that the effort to build a life is worthwhile. The credibility of any economic story depends on whether citizens can find evidence of progress in their own lives.” Promoting Security Momoh also emphasised the need for intelligence, training, coordination, and public support to strengthen security agencies in the country. “Security is an even more immediate measure. Across the country, communities face insurgent violence, banditry, kidnapping, communal conflict, farmer–pastoralist tensions and other threats. In Adamawa and the wider North-East, insecurity has disrupted homes, farming, education, livelihoods and family life,” he said. “We must speak of these realities with care. Behind every statistic is a person: a child who cannot attend school, a farmer afraid to return to a field, a family forced from its home, a community unable to reach a clinic. Justice must follow crime, and prevention must accompany response. “A government’s account of security will be judged by whether people can live, work, travel, learn and sleep without fear,” said Momoh. “These are not easy stories to tell. But a good national narrative does not hide difficult truths. It gives them names, identifies responsibility, reports what is being done, and allows citizens to see whether the response is working.” On governance, he urged political leaders to match words with action for the benefit of the citizens “Every government tells a story about its purpose. It may speak of renewal, reform, development, security or opportunity. But the public does not assess that story by the words alone. People compare it with their lived experience,” he stated. “When leaders promise a road, citizens watch to see whether it is built. When government promises relief, people ask whether it reaches those who need it. When officials announce a reform, families want to understand why it is necessary, what it will cost them, what support is available, and what success will look like. “Good communication therefore begins with the quality of the decision. If a policy has not been thought through, if its impact has not been understood, or if those who carry its cost have not been heard, communication cannot repair the weakness. It may postpone the reckoning, but it will not remove it.” “Leadership must make room for honest advice before decisions are announced. It must ask: who will benefit? Who may be harmed? What evidence supports this choice? What will we do if the expected result does not come? How will we explain the trade-offs without talking down to the public? “The public also needs to see that leaders accept responsibility. If a project is delayed, say why and give a credible timeline. If a service fails, acknowledge it and explain how the failure will be addressed. If a claim was wrong, by all means correct it. A leader’s willingness to repair a mistake can strengthen trust more than pretending the mistake never happened,” he added. Mohom commended Governor Fintiri for the achievements recorded in Adamawa. “I would like to acknowledge the work your administration is doing to transform Adamawa. Investment in roads and urban renewal, public buildings, schools and healthcare facilities is changing the state’s landscape and strengthening access to public services,” he said. “These efforts deserve recognition, and the people of Adamawa deserve a clear account of what has been completed, what is under way and what remains to be done.” He described Epelle as one who understood that communication goes beyond sending out information and encompasses the work of building understanding and confidence between an institution and the people it serves.
